title: hardening: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, the agent Git guard's Node program spawns `git` by bare name, and libuv runs <cwd>\git.exe first (it ignores NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath)
description:
Found while planning task-2f22237b. That row sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 under the marker, which cmd.exe honours (npm .cmd shims and cmd.exe children). Node's own spawn of a bare name ignores the variable: libuv's search_path looks in the spawn's cwd (else the process cwd) first, then PATH (mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first, measured 2026-10-25).

Wrapper-owned site: Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 :8267 at 717c4019) runs a Node program before every CLI launch. Its `git()` helper calls `cp.spawnSync('git', ['-C', cwd, ...])` with no cwd option, so the lookup starts in the node process's cwd. That is the seat's current directory, normally the project, so a project-root git.exe runs inside a protected seat. Check whether the sh twin's guard (prepare_agent_git_guard) uses the same program under Git Bash.

Fix direction: under the marker, give each spawnSync an absolute git, resolved by the same trusted-PATH rule as Find-MoeProtectedFile and passed in by the wrapper, or a cwd outside the project (libuv searches the spawn's cwd option). Then plant <project>\git.exe in a protected-agent-command row (Windows node.exe) and assert it never runs.

Accepted residual, document only: the agent CLI's own Node spawns (for example claude running git or rg by bare name with the project as cwd) are outside Moe's control.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, a git.exe planted at the project root never runs during the agent Git guard setup in either twin; a protected-agent-command row run through Windows node.exe proves it with a planted file.
Legacy seats are unchanged, parity-check.sh passes, and the protected-agent-command and launcher suites exit 0 on Linux and through Windows node.exe.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's protected control plane bullet names the remaining residual: bare-name spawns inside the agent CLI itself.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first, RED (test-driven-development). File: scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs, edited in the task worktree with the Edit tool. A prototype that passed against the step-2 code on Linux and through Windows node.exe is at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/52555102-plan/protected-agent-command.test.mjs.proto.diff; port it.
Read mem:gotcha-protected-agent-command-reaching-the-cli and mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first first. Re-measured on 2026-11-03: Node 22+ (libuv 1.48+) honours NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath when it is set in the SPAWNING process's own environment, and the marker already exports it. So on HEAD a project-root git.exe reached only through the current directory is already skipped. What still reaches it is a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry (any libuv), or Node 20 and older.
(a) At the end of the file add G1, for the ps1 engines only. Skip it off Windows or without GIT_DIR, like C2.
- Setup:
  - `git init -q` the fixture project with GIT_DIR's git.exe, so the guard reaches its powershell.exe ACL step.
  - Copy process.execPath to <project>\git.exe and to <project>\powershell.exe.
  - Pass NODE_OPTIONS=`--require "<logger, with / separators>"`. The logger appends JSON {pid, ppid, exe: process.execPath, args: process.argv.slice(1)}.
- The guard is the logged entry with args[0] === '-' and args[1] = the project (case-insensitive path compare). Assert it ran at least once.
- The result is the deduped, lowercased basenames of planted entries (dirname = the project) whose ppid is a guard pid. A '.' entry also reaches the launcher's own PowerShell `& git` (task-3acf7f79), so never assert on the whole log.
- Three runs, role governor, with a trusted claude.cmd stub and PATH [nodeBin, trusted, ...TAIL, GIT_DIR]:
  - marker '1' with '.' first on PATH: result [].
  - marker '1' without '.': result [].
  - legacy (marker null): result ['git.exe']. This proves the plant is reachable.
  - Both marker runs also assert exit 0 and a 'trusted claude' line in ran.log.
(b) Add G2 for bash (the `sh` engine).
- Plant <project>/git as a /bin/sh script that appends `ps -o args= -p "$PPID"` to a log and then execs realpath('/usr/bin')/git with "$@".
- PATH is [fx.project, nodeBin, trusted, ...TAIL], role governor.
- Each log line's first token basename names the parent. `ps -o comm=` prints MainThread for Node 24, so do not use it.
- marker '1' must have no 'node' parent; legacy must have one. Both runs exit 0.
(c) In the C1/C2 header comment, replace "(Node's own spawn of a bare name does not)" with an accurate clause: Node 22+ honours the variable too, which G1 covers.
RED proof, against the unchanged wrappers:
- G1 through Windows node.exe: the '.' run fails with actual ['git.exe'].
- G2 on Linux fails with parents 'bash,node'.
- Run both from a scratch copy, `git archive HEAD scripts docs package.json` plus your test file. Put the copy under /mnt/c/Users/<u>/AppData/Local/Temp for the Windows rows, and run Windows node.exe from a normal WSL shell, not env -i. Paste both RED test tails into the step notes.

Implementation in both wrappers (Edit tool, task worktree). The reference diffs passed G1, G2, the full gate and parity: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/52555102-plan/moe-agent.ps1.proto.diff and moe-agent.sh.proto.diff.
(a) The guard program text, byte-identical and ASCII in both. agent-git-guard.test.mjs's twin test compares the two, and PS 5.1 pipes this text to node.
- `const [project, temp, gitCmd] = process.argv.slice(-3)`.
- After `const env`, a 2-line comment and `const strict = process.env.MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED === '1';`. The comment says nothing runs by bare name under the marker: Node looks one up in the current directory or through '.'/relative/in-project PATH entries, so the wrapper passes git's absolute path (task-52555102).
- The `git` helper spawns gitCmd.
- Right after the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT check: `if (strict && !path.isAbsolute(gitCmd)) throw Error('path');`.
- In the win block: `const powershell = strict ? path.join(process.env.SystemRoot || '', 'System32', 'WindowsPowerShell', 'v1.0', 'powershell.exe') : 'powershell.exe';`, then `if (strict && !path.isAbsolute(powershell)) throw Error('path');`, and spawn `powershell`.
(b) ps1 Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard, before the OutputEncoding try:
- `$guardGit = 'git'`.
- Under $script:MoeRuntimeProtected:
  - `$gitExtensions = if ($PSVersionTable.PSEdition -ne 'Core' -or $IsWindows) { @('.exe') } else { @('') }`;
  - `$guardGit = Find-MoeProtectedFile 'git' $gitExtensions`;
  - `if (-not $guardGit) { throw 'MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED: refusing to launch an unprotected CLI' }`.
- Pass `$guardGit` as the third native argument after `([IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + '.')`. The path ends in .exe, so PS 5.1's trailing-backslash quoting is not an issue.
(c) sh:
- `agent_git_guard_node() { # $1 = the git the program runs`, with "$1" added after "$SECURE_TEMP_DIR".
- In prepare_agent_git_guard: `local entry guard_git=git`; when RUNTIME_PROTECTED = 1, `guard_git=$(protected_path_lookup git "$(normalize_path "$PROJECT")" .exe) || return 1`; then `AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT=$(agent_git_guard_node "$guard_git") || return 1`. The `.exe` argument applies only to msys/cygwin, and Node cannot spawn a .cmd.
(d) Correct the two NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath comments (ps1 :470-472, sh :52-54), identically. "Node's own spawn of a bare name ignores it." becomes: Node 22+ (libuv 1.48+) honours it too, read from its own environment; older Node does not, and no lookup skips a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry.
Error handling: no trusted git refuses the launch with the existing MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED (today a missing git fails the same way), and the program refuses a non-absolute git or powershell under the marker. Legacy passes 'git' and spawns 'powershell.exe' exactly as before.
Keep moe-agent.ps1 UTF-8 with a BOM and LF line endings. Then run G1 and G2 (GREEN), plus `node --test scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs` on Linux, which exercises the legacy guard paths, about 80 s.

Docs (DoD 3). In docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's **Protected control plane** bullet, replace the sentence "Both export `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` ... because libuv ignores that variable." (:421-423). Keep the wrap at about 118 columns. The new text says:
- cmd.exe (an npm `.cmd` shim or any cmd.exe in the seat) and Node 22+ (libuv 1.48+, which reads the variable from the spawning process) never look a bare name up in the current directory, the project.
- Older Node still does, and no lookup skips a `.`, relative or in-project PATH entry.
- So the agent Git guard's Node program gets git's absolute path, from an absolute PATH entry outside the project, and runs `%SystemRoot%`'s `powershell.exe`. With no such git, the guard refuses the launch (MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED).
- The remaining residual is the agent CLI's own bare-name spawns. They inherit the variable, but Moe controls neither the CLI's PATH walk nor a CLI runtime that ignores it.
- The launchers' own lookups through such PATH entries are open: task-0b2ea570 (sh) and task-3acf7f79 (ps1).
Use no daemonGitDocs phrase ("never runs git" and similar), and check each claim against the step-2 code.

Verification (DoD 2). Run ONE command, once and fresh, from the task worktree in a normal WSL shell: the three executionContract.checkRefs pieces joined with ' && '. Only the Linux leg runs under env -i, because the Windows node.exe leg needs the Windows PATH with git carried through interop. That joined command and its output tail are the complete_task evidence.
The launcher harnesses run in place; the rails allow that, and each suite sets MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER.
Planner dry run on the prototype at HEAD 5c5b3706:
- Linux: 187 tests, 159 pass, 0 fail, 28 skipped, 77 s.
- Windows: 249 tests, 208 pass, 0 fail, 41 skipped, 189 s.
- ParseFile exit 0, parity-check PASS.
Counts move with HEAD; exit 0 is the gate.
The agent-git-guard suite alone is 28 tests and about 80 s on Linux. On Windows it runs in the same leg, about 3 min. If an unrelated row fails, rerun that file alone and check `uptime` before reporting it; never edit it.

Adversarial self-review (load the adversarial-self-review skill), on `git diff "$(git merge-base HEAD "${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-HEAD}")"` plus the working tree. Check:
- The two program copies are identical and ASCII (run the twin test).
- Legacy argv is unchanged apart from the extra 'git' argument.
- A path with spaces or brackets in $projectPath, the temp dir or the git path still passes through PS 5.1 native quoting.
- No new MOE_ code exists (parity).
- The docs claims are exact.
Mutants, in the scratch copy. Back up once, restore and cmp before citing. Count a kill only when a row fails on its assertion:
- M1: ps1 passes 'git' instead of $guardGit. G1 '.' run is RED.
- M2: sh passes git instead of "$guard_git". G2 is RED.
- M3: the program spawns a bare 'powershell.exe' under strict. G1 '.' run is RED, with ['powershell.exe'] as a guard child.
- M4: Find-MoeProtectedFile is replaced with (Get-Command git).Source. G1 '.' run is RED.
- M5: the program's strict absolute-path check is removed. It may survive (defense in depth); say so.
Size: expect about +110 net lines, most of them the two test rows. Record the mutant table and any residual in the completion summary. Declare the four files as modifiedFiles.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, the agent Git guard's Node program, the same text in moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh, spawns git only by the absolute path the wrapper resolved from an absolute PATH entry outside the project. That is Find-MoeProtectedFile in ps1 and protected_path_lookup in sh. On Windows it spawns powershell.exe only as %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe.
A git.exe or powershell.exe planted at the project root therefore never runs as a child of the guard, whether it would be reached through the current directory or through a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry. With no trusted git, the launch is refused with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED.
Legacy seats pass 'git' and spawn 'powershell.exe' exactly as before. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states the corrected libuv behavior and the agent CLI residual.
acceptanceCriteria: G1, on PS 5.1 and PS 7 through Windows node.exe: under the marker, with and without a '.' PATH entry, no planted git.exe or powershell.exe runs as a child of the guard, the launch exits 0 and the CLI runs. In legacy the planted git.exe does run as a guard child.
G2, bash on Linux: under the marker, a planted <project>/git reached through an in-project PATH entry never has the guard's node as its parent. In legacy it does.
The Linux and Windows launcher suites, ParseFile, parity-check and lint all exit 0.
The docs bullet names the agent CLI's own bare-name spawns as the residual and corrects the libuv claim.
invariants: Under the marker the guard program never spawns a bare name, and it refuses a non-absolute git or powershell path.
The guard program text is byte-identical and ASCII in both wrappers.
Legacy behavior, argv apart from the extra 'git' argument, and refusal codes are unchanged. No new MOE_ code.
compatibility: agent-git-guard.test.mjs still passes unchanged: it covers the legacy guard paths and the twin-program equality.
PS 5.1 native argument passing for paths with spaces stays intact (the new argument ends in .exe).
approvedScope: The guard program (gitCmd argument, strict marker check, absolute powershell), Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard ($guardGit), agent_git_guard_node and prepare_agent_git_guard (guard_git), and the two NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath comments.
protected-agent-command.test.mjs: rows G1 and G2, and the C1/C2 header comment.
reuse: Find-MoeProtectedFile and protected_path_lookup, rather than a new resolver.
The C2 row's fixture pattern: governor role, GIT_DIR, node.exe copies as planted files.
sourceAssumptions: scripts/moe-agent.ps1: Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard (~:8274) pipes the program into `& node - $projectPath ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + '.')`. Under the marker, node is Set-Alias'd to $script:MoeNode (~:567).

scripts/moe-agent.sh: agent_git_guard_node (~:8653) runs "$NODE_CMD" - "$PROJECT" "$SECURE_TEMP_DIR". prepare_agent_git_guard (~:8717) is called at ~:10126, which prints MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED on failure.
Find-MoeProtectedFile (ps1 ~:528) and protected_path_lookup (sh ~:537) implement the trusted-PATH rule.
libuv 1.48+ skips the cwd when NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath is in the spawning process's environment, and walks PATH entries regardless (measured 2026-11-03).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Each alternative was rejected:
(1) A spawn `cwd` outside the project. libuv still walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, so it does not stop a planted git.
(2) Rewriting PATH early under the marker. That is broader (task-0b2ea570 for sh, task-3acf7f79 for ps1) and does not cover Node 20 and older, which search the cwd anyway.
(3) Re-implementing the trusted-PATH rule in JS. That would be a third copy of Find-MoeProtectedFile and protected_path_lookup, and it would drift from task-89579137's alias fix.
(4) Making powershell.exe absolute in legacy too. The DoD says legacy is unchanged.
(5) A whole-log G1 assertion. A '.' entry also reaches the launcher's own PowerShell `& git`, which is filed as task-3acf7f79. Counting only the guard's children is exactly what the DoD asks.
The worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs (also bare git) are out of this DoD and are in task-3acf7f79.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Planner measurements, 2026-11-03:
- libuv src/win/process.c search_path has called NeedCurrentDirectoryForExePathW(L"") since v1.48.0 (absent in 1.47.0). It reads the CALLING process's own env, and any value, even '', turns the cwd search off.
- Node 22.23 has libuv 1.51 and Node 24.16 has 1.52 (both honour it). Node 20.20 has 1.46 (does not).
- The 2026-10-25 memory, and 2f22237b's comments and docs, wrongly said that libuv ignores it; that probe set it only in the child's env. Both memories are now corrected.
How the wrappers behave:
- Under the marker, the ps1 aliases node to the absolute $script:MoeNode, and sh pins NODE_CMD, so only git and powershell.exe were bare inside the guard.
- prepare_agent_git_guard failing makes the caller print MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and exit 1. The ps1 throw propagates the same way.
planningNotes.risks:
Test hazards:
- NODE_OPTIONS reaches every node in the seat, so the logger must never throw. It only appends.
- G1 needs the fixture to be a Git repository, or the guard exits before its powershell.exe step.
- The harness PATH (TAIL) has no WindowsPowerShell, so an unfixed guard in a repository fails on ENOENT. Expected.
- The sh twin under Git Bash cannot run in this suite ("Git Bash rewrites PATH"). It relies on MSYS argv conversion of '/c/...' paths, the same conversion it already relies on for $PROJECT and the temp dir.
Overlapping rows:
- 408a0ac1 (REVIEW) changed the same `& node -` line, hence the dependsOn.
- 0b2ea570 and 89579137 now wait on this row (same test file and docs bullet).
- 3acf7f79 waits on this row and on 0b2ea570.
